kind: controlled visual comparison, not a latency benchmark or a human-subject study
fixture: deterministic Person-NNNN identifiers; ring plus offset-7 edges, exactly two directed edges per vertex; average undirected degree four
zoom: Fit Center, then two Zoom In clicks (1.25 squared = 1.5625 times fitted zoom)

observations.30: Node identifiers and relationship labels are readable in a local view; zoom crops the overview.
observations.50: Node identifiers remain readable in a local view; some edge/label crossings require attention.
observations.100: Identifiers are visibly small; suitable for orientation, not comfortable reading at this camera setting.
observations.300: Node labels are hidden after the same two zoom clicks; view communicates topology rather than identities.
observations.500: Node labels remain hidden and edges are denser.
observations.1000: Node labels remain hidden and local crossings are substantially denser.

recommendation: For this viewport, label length and degree-four fixture, use about 30-50 vertices for everyday detailed reading; 100 is an expanded overview. The current 1000 ceiling is a resource guard, not a readability guarantee. This comparison does not change the implemented default 300 / ceiling 1000 settings.
limitations: One deterministic synthetic topology, one viewport, one layout and label policy; no human participants. Current automatic label visibility also depends on total node+edge count and absolute zoom. Results cannot establish a universal limit for every graph.
